questions.question: What is "clickbait"?
options: Sensational headlines designed to get clicks, not to tell the truth
A computer virus
A fact-checking website
A type of advertisement for fishing gear
questions.explanation: Clickbait headlines like "You won't BELIEVE what happened!" are designed to attract clicks rather than inform accurately.

questions.question: What is a deepfake?
options: AI-generated video or audio that looks and sounds real
A very deep ocean documentary
A long article with many sources
An anonymous news source
questions.explanation: Deepfakes are AI-generated videos or audio that convincingly imitate real people, making it harder to trust what we see.

questions.question: What is a filter bubble?
options: A situation where algorithms only show you content that matches your existing views
A tool for cleaning your screen
A photo filter on social media
A way to block all advertisements
questions.explanation: Filter bubbles occur when algorithms feed you content matching your existing views, so you rarely see other perspectives. Echo chambers reinforce this.

questions.question: What is "cherry-picking" in arguments and news?
options: Selecting only the information that supports your own view
Choosing the healthiest food options
Reading several different sources
Quoting all sides of a debate
questions.explanation: Cherry-picking means presenting only the evidence that supports your view while ignoring the rest.

questions.question: Why do social media algorithms matter for what you believe?
options: They decide what content you see, which can shape your view of the world
They have no influence on users
They only affect advertisements
They always show balanced news
questions.explanation: Algorithms choose what appears in your feed based on engagement, which can amplify extreme content and narrow your worldview.
